title: Gurren Lagann UK Collectors Blu-rays Released on Monday
content:
The two Gurren Lagann feature films are Gurren Lagann the Movie –Childhood's End- , (compiled from the 15 TV episodes with some new footage) and Gurren Lagann the Movie – The Lights in the Sky Are Stars (a sequel to the series).

The two UHD Blu-ray discs will contain the films in 4K HDR10, featuring the original Japanese audio (with English subtitles) and the English dub tracks, both in Dolby Atmos. There will also be Japanese stereo audio commentaries for the films from the production crew, subtitled in English.

The standard Blu-ray discs have been reauthored to include the films' English dubs, as well as the Japanese audio with English subtitles. Both will be presented in 5.1 DTS-HD Master Audio. The subtitled Japanese audio commentaries will be included in stereo DTS-HD Master Audio.

The Collector's Edition slipcase will feature new artwork created for the15th anniversary Japanese re-release of the films. The edition will also contain two art cards.

Also on August 31, Anime Limited will release a standard Blu-ray edition of the films, also including the English dub and the other on-disc contents from the Collector's Edition.

The Gurren Lagann series is set on a future Earth where people are forced to live in isolated underground villages. One boy uncovers a key to a robot, and the resulting adventures put him in the battles waging on the surface and lead him to the secrets behind humanity's new existence.

"Karasuno made it to the Spring High preliminary finals, but waiting for them is Shiratorizawa Academy and their ace who played for the national team! To counter this powerhouse, the crows must learn a new playstyle in the midst of this do-or-die match."

"Kazuya's romantic plans reach new heights when he invites Chizuru on his family's vacation. But his dream trip and planned confession leads to chaos when Mami shows up at the resort. Will Chizuru hear his feelings in this war zone of love?"
author: ANN

title: Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd and Pichu Stop-Motion Series' Trailer Streams in India
content:
The official Pokémon YouTube channel began streaming the trailer for Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd and Pichu , the franchise 's stop-motion animated series collaboration with independent studio Aardman ( Wallace & Gromit , Shaun the Sheep ), on Friday. The Pokémon Company announced on Friday Disney+ will exclusively stream the series worldwide. It is currently unclear if JioHotstar will also stream the series.

The below trailer is available to view worldwide, including in India.

The series will debut in 2027. The Disney XD channel will debut the series on television in North America.

The series is part of a global distribution deal between Disney+ and The Pokémon Company International . The deal also includes Pokémon the Series: The Beginning , the original Indigo League season of the anime, which is already streaming on JioHotstar in India along with 17 other seasons of the anime.

Peter Lord, Cofounder and Creative Director at Aardman , stated that the Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch'd and Pichu animated series will take place in a region that is "very close to our hearts." The video teases Wooloo and Sirfetch'd, which are Pokémon originally introduced in the Pokémon Sword/Shield games that are set in the Galar region based on the U.K.

Tom Parkinson is the director, Natalie McKay is the creative director, and James Young is the creative lead.

Pokémon Concierge , another stop-motion animated series for the Pokémon franchise , debuted with four episodes on Netflix in December 2023. The anime streamed in India at the same time in Japanese and also with English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu dubs. The stop-motion production company dwarf studios ( Rilakkuma and Kaoru ) animated the episodes thus far. New episodes premiered in September 2025.

The Pokémon: Horizons anime premiered in Japan in April 2023 with a one-hour first-episode special. The show airs in Japan on Fridays at 6:55 p.m. JST. The anime premiered on Indian television on Hungama in May 2024. It aired with new original opening and ending themes performed by Armaan Malik and Shirley Setia and composed by Vishal-Sheykhar. The Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali YouTube channels for Pokémon Asia began streaming the respective local language dubs of the Pokémon Horizons: The Series anime on YouTube in July 2024.

Netflix premiered Pokémon Horizons: The Series —The Search for Laqua , the anime's second season, in North America in February 2025. The English YouTube channel for Pokémon South Asia began streaming the English dub of the season on December 19. Netflix added Pokémon Horizons: Season 3—Rising Hope in North America on January 6.

title: Hindi Dubs of Reincarnated as a Slime Season 4, 'Welcome to Demon School, Iruma-kun' Season 3 Stream on Muse India
content:
The new season of That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime debuted on April 3 on NTV 's now one-hour "Friday Anime Night" programming block, at 11:00 p.m. JST. The new season started airing on BS11 on April 4 at 10:00 p.m. JST and on other streaming services at 11:00 p.m. JST. Crunchyroll is streaming the anime in India as it airs.

8-Bit is returning once again to animate the fourth season, and Miho Okasaki returns to voice protagonist Rimuru Tempest. Eir Aoi performed the first opening theme song "Esoragoto" (Pipe Dream), and CiON performed the first ending theme song "Katsubō" (Craving). Daoko performs the current opening theme song "TACTIC," and Azusa Tadokoro performs the current ending theme song "Hymnal."

The anime's fourth season will air for a total run of five cours (quarters of a year), with the first two cours airing continuously.

The third season includes returning main staff members. Makoto Moriwaki returned to direct the third season at Bandai Namco Pictures , and Kazuyuki Fudeyasu once again was charge of series composition. Yumiko Hara was the new character designer. Akimitsu Honma once again composed the music.

The anime's fourth season debuted on April 4. Crunchyroll is streaming it in India as it airs in Japan. The season will have 24 episodes that will run for two cours .

The first anime premiered in October 2019 on NHK Educational , and had 23 episodes. The second season premiered in April 2021. Netflix is streaming both seasons in India.

Osamu Nishi launched the manga in Akita Shoten 's Weekly Shōnen Champion magazine in March 2017.

title: 'Ao Ashi Season 2' Unveils Additional Staff, First Promo
content:
The official website for the Ao Ashi television anime series unveiled additional staff, and the first promotional video on Tuesday. The anime sequel adapting Yuugo Kobayashi 's sports manga is scheduled to premiere on October 4 at 5:00 p.m. on NHK-E.

Staff Chief Animation Director: Manabu Nakatake ( Ao Ashi ), Asami Taguchi ( Lupin Zero ), Junko Yamanaka ( Kono Oto Tomare! ) Action Animation Director: Tadayoshi Okimura ( Blue Lock vs. U-20 Japan ), Satoshi Kubo ( Ao Ashi ) Art Design: Yuuki Shigekawa ( Komi-san wa, Comyushou desu. 2nd Season ) Art Director: Niki Higaki ( Sanda ) Color Design: Hiromi Miyawaki ( Baki ) CG Director: Kaito Iwata ( Sylvanian Families: Freya no Piece of Secret ) Director of Photography: Jirou Tazawa ( Cheat Kusushi no Slow Life: Isekai ni Tsukurou Drugstore ) Editing: Masato Yoshitake ( Dungeon Meshi )

Rock band 10-FEET ( The First Slam Dunk , Uma Musume: Cinderella Gray Part 2 ) is performing the opening theme "Fortress Defense" and singer-songwriter Ai Higuchi ( Shingeki no Kyojin: The Final Season Part 2 , Snowball Earth ) performs the ending theme "Triangle." Both theme songs are previewed in the promotional video below.

Kazuki Yokoyama ( Blue Lock episode director) directs the new season at TMS Entertainment and Masahiro Yokotani ( Make Heroine ga Oosugiru! ) is handling the series composition. Manabu Nakatake, Asami Taguchi, and Junko Yamanaka are designing the characters. Masaru Yokoyama ( Mashle ) is composing the music.

Kobayashi began drawing the manga based on Naohiko Ueno 's original draft in Big Comic Spirits in January 2015 and ended its serialization in June 2025. Shogakukan published the 40th and final volume in August 2025.

title: 'With You, Our Love Will Make it Through' Manga Ends in 13th Volume
content:
Chihiro Yuzuki announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Monday that her With You, Our Love Will Make it Through ( Kimi to Koete Koi ni Naru ) manga will end with the 13th compiled book volume.

Yen Press is releasing the manga in English, and it describes the story:

When high schooler Mari bumps into a fellow tardy student, she's surprised to find out he's a beastfolk who's to attend her school! After all, it's not rare for beastfolk to coexist alongside humans, but it's still uncommon, with the prejudice and all. Nervous to meet one at first, Mari soon learns there's more to him than his furry exterior. In fact, the more she gets to know him, the more she finds herself drawn to him, his steadfastness, his kindheartedness, and…his body…

Yuzuki launched the manga on Shueisha 's Manga Mee shojo manga website in May 2019, and it is ongoing. Shueisha published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on March 24, and will ship the 12th volume on September 25.

The anime adaptation debuted in October 2025 on the Tokyo MX channel. Crunchyroll streamed the series as it aired, and also streamed an English dub .

title: Aoashi Season 2 Main Trailer Previews Theme Song, October 4 Premiere Revealed
content:
The upcoming second season of AOASHI has unveiled its main trailer, featuring the new theme songs ahead of the anime’s October 4 premiere. Studio TMS Entertainment was previously confirmed to be taking over from Production I.G for the animation production.

The first cour will cover the opening 12 episodes of the season’s planned 24-episode run. Season 2’s opening theme is performed by Japanese rock band 10-FEET, while singer-songwriter Ai Higuchi performs the ending theme. Both of the songs are featured in the new trailer, which you can watch below.

You can also see the previously revealed main visual for the anime below.

Aoashi (stylized AO ASHI ) by Yugo Kobayashi began in January 2015 and was serialized in Shogakukan’s Weekly Big Comic Spirits magazine. The manga recently exceeded 20 million circulating copies and ended with 40 volumes . The first season by Production I.G ran for 22 episodes from April to September 2022. Crunchyroll is streaming it, describing the story: After a loss in his last junior high school soccer tourney, Ehime Prefecture’s ace player, Ashito Aoi, is devastated but in every loss there’s a victory. Tatsuya Fukuda, manager of an organization that trains students for one of the leading clubs in the J-League, sees Ashito’s raw talent and offers a tryout to his group. Together they’ll bring the youth club and Aoshi’s talents to new heights!

title: Toshiko Machida's Hanako-gari Manga Ends
content:
Kodansha 's Pocket Magazine platform published the final chapter of Toshiko Machida 's Hanako-gari (Hanako Hunt) manga on August 27.

The story is set in a world where spirits run rampant. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government establishes an organization meant to search for and protect these spirits, renamed "Hanako," but the truth is the government is hunting and disposing of these spirits.

Machida launched the series on Kodansha 's Pocket Magazine platform in September 2025. Kodansha shipped the second compiled book volume on March 9, and will release the third and final volume on September 9.

Machida's The Demon Consort: "I Love You" Are Frightening Words manga ended in April 2025. The series launched on NTT Solmare 's Comic CMOA platform in March 2024. Shinchosha shipped the third and final volume in August 2025. Yen Press publishes the series in English, and shipped the first volume on August 25.

title: bilibili App Relaunches Globally Without ID Verification
content:
The Chinese streaming service bilibili relaunched a global version of its app on Android on August 19. The new app does not require identity verification when posting overseas, which the previous app required, and is reportedly mixing Chinese and International content. The company plans to launch the app on iOS and in other countries soon.

bilibili partnered with Aniplex on the animated project To Be Hero X , which premiered in April 2025. Crunchyroll is streaming To Be Hero X worldwide excluding Asia. The series streams in Japan on Netflix and Amazon Prime Video .

The company acquired Shanghai-based animation company Haoliners Cultures Media Co., Ltd., including Haoliners' Japanese subsidiary Emon Animation Company in February 2021.

The company bilibili was founded in 2009, and it is China's largest streaming platform for Japanese animation, above TencentVideo and iQIYI . The company streams anime titles and also invests in anime productions. The website also includes Chinese animation and user-uploaded content. The service collects both advertising revenue and pay-per-view subscription charges.

American anime publisher Funimation and bilibili jointly announced a partnership to acquire anime licenses in March 2019. For the partnership, both companies are jointly acquiring licenses "over the next few years," including IP rights for broadcast television, video-on-demand, electronic sell-through, home entertainment, gaming, and merchandise in the United States and China.

Sony Corporation of America paid approximately US$400 million in 2020 to buy 17.3 million shares of bilibili , amounting to 4.98% of the Chinese company's stock. The companies plan to collaborate on projects in the Chinese entertainment market, including animation and mobile games, after signing their business contract.

title: Pokemon: Wild Card Proves Ash Might Never Come Back (And That’s Ok)
content:
Pokemon: Wild Card is the first time that we’ve seen a Pokemon movie in years, with the previous example being Pokemon: Secrets of the Jungle back in 2020. This recent film wasn’t just the last time that the franchise hit the big screen in Japan; it was the last film led by Ash Ketchum. While we can’t say with one hundred percent certainty that Ketchum won’t find some way to make an appearance, it seems as though Wild Card is looking to explore a very different side of this universe. With many fans originally believing that Ash might return via a new movie, it seems that said fans have been proven wrong, and maybe this is for the best.

Ironically enough, Pokémon: Wild Card not only doesn’t focus on Ash and Pikachu, but it will also focus on a Pokémon Trading Card Game player in the anime’s universe. We know this thanks to the initial trailer highlighting a seemingly new character who is spending the runtime with his pocket monster partner, Mimikyu. To date, no anime episode or movie in the franchise has specifically focused on the card game, or even hinted at the idea that it was a part of this universe. Not even bringing in Liko and Roy, the current stars of Pokémon: Horizons , Wild Card is making a drastic change from what we’ve seen in the past, and this might be the best way forward.

This Wild Card is Ash-Less

Wild Card exploring a wildly new part of the franchise via the card game is a risky take, but it’s one the franchise needs. Even with Roy and Liko making some big changes to the television series, returning to Ash might feel like a retread for many. This isn’t to say we should never see Ketchum make a comeback, but letting his absence breathe a little longer would be the right decision. After all, it’s only been a little over three years since Ash left the anime, so taking a wild swing, even if unsuccessful, is a worthwhile risk.

Ash, for those who need a refresher, finally achieved his goal of becoming the greatest Pokémon trainer in the world in the past anime series, Pokémon Ultimate Journeys: The Series . While he still continued his journey to try to discover the true meaning of being a trainer, his conclusion has opened the door for new, off-the-beaten-path stories to take place. Luckily, this doesn’t entirely mean that the door is completely closed in relation to Ash.

In 2024, The Pokemon Company’s Head of Media Production, Andy Goes, left the door open for a potential return of Ash. Specifically, Goes stated, “We’ve said farewell. Ash is still in the world. Anything is possible , I suppose. In the world of Pokemon, there are so many possibilities. We hope Ash and Pikachu continue in their journey. Their journey is ongoing somewhere in the Pokemon world. It’s totally up to our fans’ imagination. For the time being, we would love to focus on the new story of Liko and Roy. Horizons invites a new beginning.” Certainly, if a movie were to eventually focus on an older Ash as he marched alongside Pikachu in the world at large, that would make for a grand story, but saving that story for the right moment feels like the right call.

contentBlocks.text: Pokemon: Wild Card is the first time that we’ve seen a Pokemon movie in years, with the previous example being Pokemon: Secrets of the Jungle back in 2020. This recent film wasn’t just the last time that the franchise hit the big screen in Japan; it was the last film led by Ash Ketchum. While we can’t say with one hundred percent certainty that Ketchum won’t find some way to make an appearance, it seems as though Wild Card is looking to explore a very different side of this universe. With many fans originally believing that Ash might return via a new movie, it seems that said fans have been proven wrong, and maybe this is for the best.

Ironically enough, Pokémon: Wild Card not only doesn’t focus on Ash and Pikachu, but it will also focus on a Pokémon Trading Card Game player in the anime’s universe. We know this thanks to the initial trailer highlighting a seemingly new character who is spending the runtime with his pocket monster partner, Mimikyu. To date, no anime episode or movie in the franchise has specifically focused on the card game, or even hinted at the idea that it was a part of this universe. Not even bringing in Liko and Roy, the current stars of Pokémon: Horizons , Wild Card is making a drastic change from what we’ve seen in the past, and this might be the best way forward.
This Wild Card is Ash-Less

Wild Card exploring a wildly new part of the franchise via the card game is a risky take, but it’s one the franchise needs. Even with Roy and Liko making some big changes to the television series, returning to Ash might feel like a retread for many. This isn’t to say we should never see Ketchum make a comeback, but letting his absence breathe a little longer would be the right decision. After all, it’s only been a little over three years since Ash left the anime, so taking a wild swing, even if unsuccessful, is a worthwhile risk.

Ash, for those who need a refresher, finally achieved his goal of becoming the greatest Pokémon trainer in the world in the past anime series, Pokémon Ultimate Journeys: The Series . While he still continued his journey to try to discover the true meaning of being a trainer, his conclusion has opened the door for new, off-the-beaten-path stories to take place. Luckily, this doesn’t entirely mean that the door is completely closed in relation to Ash.

In 2024, The Pokemon Company’s Head of Media Production, Andy Goes, left the door open for a potential return of Ash. Specifically, Goes stated, “We’ve said farewell. Ash is still in the world. Anything is possible , I suppose. In the world of Pokemon, there are so many possibilities. We hope Ash and Pikachu continue in their journey. Their journey is ongoing somewhere in the Pokemon world. It’s totally up to our fans’ imagination. For the time being, we would love to focus on the new story of Liko and Roy. Horizons invites a new beginning.” Certainly, if a movie were to eventually focus on an older Ash as he marched alongside Pikachu in the world at large, that would make for a grand story, but saving that story for the right moment feels like the right call.
